en: The Philippine eagle, our national bird, lays only one egg per breeding season, making it highly vulnerable to extinction.
Marcela Agoncillo and her daughters hand-sewed the first official Philippine flag in Hong Kong before the 1898 independence proclamation.
Unlike many countries, the Philippine President serves a single six-year term and is constitutionally banned from seeking re-election.
The T'boli people of South Cotabato create intricate T'nalak cloth by weaving patterns they see in their dreams.
Dr. Fe del Mundo invented a bamboo incubator for rural areas, significantly reducing infant mortality in the Philippines.
Ancient Filipinos wrote on bamboo and leaves using Baybayin, a pre-colonial script where every symbol represents a complete syllable.
The MassKara Festival in Bacolod City was created in 1980 to uplift the spirits of locals during a severe economic crisis.
National hero Jose Rizal popularized the term "Filipino" to include all archipelago inhabitants, rather than just Spaniards born in the islands.
Under the Philippine Constitution, every citizen has the right to a balanced and healthful ecology in harmony with nature.
The Waling-waling, often called the "Queen of Philippine Orchids," grows exclusively high up in the branches of tall forest trees.
National Artist Fernando Amorsolo revolutionized Philippine painting by perfecting a unique backlighting technique that makes his rural scenes glow.
The Filipino tradition of "pagmamano" involves pressing an elder's hand to one's forehead to say "mano po" and receive a blessing.
